scope: OpenCode request/response/session semantics, errors, history/status interpretation and compatibility assumptions (src/providers/opencode.ts and its consumers in src/coordinator.ts, src/domain.ts) against @opencode-ai/sdk@1.18.31

findings.title: An unrecognized /session/status response shape is read as 'the turn finished', silently completing a worker mid-generation
findings.evidence: inspect() reads sessionStatus(status.data?.[w.opencode_session_id]?.type). For any body that is not a record keyed by session id (null, array, string, non-status body) the index yields undefined and sessionStatus() returns 'idle' at line 184, which coordinator.ts:560 treats as settled. The adapter is strict only about an unrecognized 'type' (-> 'unknown'); the body shape is never validated. src/config.ts:44 leaves the worker-side server unpinned (bare 'opencode serve'), so the shape is an external contract.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev28/probes/probe1-status-shape.ts (real OpenCodeAgent + Coordinator, in-process fake fetch): statuses for a genuinely busy session -> 'absent key -> idle', 'null body -> idle', 'array body -> idle', 'string body -> idle', 'unrecognized type -> unknown'. Coordinator impact: fake server reports busy with one completed reply and a second assistant turn still streaming -> baseline state=running (correct), but with an array-shaped status body -> state=completed result="FIRST".
findings.recommendation: Validate the body before reading it: return 'unknown' when data is null, not an object, or an array; only treat a well-formed record missing this session's key as 'idle'. Update the 'null body -> idle' assertion in tests/session-status.test.ts to expect 'unknown'.
findings.confidence: high (behavior reproduced against the target code; only the environmental trigger is inferred)

findings.title: Every poll re-walks the entire session history: uncapped, uncached, order-assuming
findings.evidence: inspect() loops 'while (page.length === 100)' walking every older page and unshifting them, with no page cap and no per-worker memo; monitor() calls it on every tick. Requests per inspect grow linearly with history. One failed page (throwOnError: true) discards the entire snapshot.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev28/probes/probe2-pagination.ts: 100 messages -> 3 requests/37ms; 1000 -> 12/178ms; 5000 -> 52/829ms; 20000 -> 202/3262ms (15ms simulated RTT). Three polls of a 5000-message session -> 156 requests. A server that returns an overlapping page makes inspect() throw 'OpenCode message pagination did not advance'; probe3 shows the coordinator then keeps the worker non-terminal in state=running with 'Provider or OpenCode operation failed; retrying within deadline' until the deadline.
findings.recommendation: Cache the oldest fetched message id per worker and fetch forward only; cap the backward walk (the coordinator only needs messages parented to the current dispatch message id); degrade to the recent page on a page-fetch failure instead of throwing.
findings.confidence: high for the cost and the wedge (measured); the cursor's lexicographic-order assumption (sort()[0] == oldest, src/store.ts:217 mixes SwarmForge message ids into the same namespace) is an unverified hypothesis

findings.title: OpenCode error detail is discarded and errored messages without time.completed are dropped entirely
findings.evidence: The adapter maps 'error: info.error?.name'. At the pinned SDK the diagnosis lives in info.error.data (ApiError: message/statusCode/isRetryable; ProviderAuthError: providerID/message; StructuredOutputError: retries; see @opencode-ai/sdk@1.18.31 dist/v2/gen/types.gen.d.ts). coordinator.ts:597 then reports only 'OpenCode session failed (<Name>)'. Separately coordinator.ts:581-584 requires m.completed, so an errored assistant message lacking time.completed is excluded from 'replies' and the worker later dies with the unrelated 'No token progress' message.
findings.reproduction: Code trace against the pinned SDK type definitions; no server needed. redactorFor(this).value is already applied to results at coordinator.ts:707, so a redacted data.message could be surfaced.
findings.recommendation: Carry a bounded, redacted info.error.data.message through AgentMessage.error and include it in the failure string; treat info.error !== undefined as terminal even without time.completed.
findings.confidence: high for the discarded detail (code + pinned SDK types); the no-time.completed branch is an unverified hypothesis about server behavior

findings.title: A saved session that no longer exists fails the worker as 'Provisioning timed out' instead of being recreated
findings.evidence: When w.opencode_session_id is set, ensureSession calls session.get and returns it; with throwOnError: true a 404/410 throws, so the deterministic-title search and session.create fallback a few lines below are never reached. step() retries every tick while 'booting' and the provisioning timeout at coordinator.ts:446-449 then fails the worker with an error naming the wrong subsystem.
findings.reproduction: /tmp/rev28/probes/probe3-impact.ts: ensureSession throwing 'HTTP 404: /session/ses-1 not found' -> 'state=booting error="Provider or OpenCode operation failed; retrying within deadline"'; after the provision timeout -> 'state=failed error="Provisioning timed out"'.
findings.recommendation: Catch the not-found case specifically (the SDK error carries the HTTP status) and fall through to session.list/session.create; keep rethrowing transport and auth failures.
findings.confidence: high (reproduced against the target coordinator and adapter with fakes)

tests.bun_version: 1.4.2 (installed at /tmp/rev28/bunhome; snapshot bun 1.3.14 cannot read lockfileVersion 2)

limitations: Full test suite deliberately not run (whole-suite scope); only the three in-scope test files.
No real OpenCode server, model provider or network smoke: all adapter/coordinator probes used in-process fake fetch and a fake WorkerProvider.

Server-side message ordering versus the lexicographic 'before' cursor, and whether OpenCode stamps time.completed on an errored message, could not be verified from the SDK package and are reported as hypotheses.
The OpenCode server version in the worker image is external to this repo, so the likelihood of the /session/status shape change in F1 is unverified; only the resulting code behavior was reproduced.
Experiments live only under /tmp/rev28 (pristine detached clone at the target, a runnable copy, the unpacked SDK, and three probe scripts); /workspace/repo was never modified.
